title.zh: 卷60 志三十五 地理七 山西
title.raw: 卷60 志三十五 地理七 山西

translations.literal: Shanxi
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi

translations.literal: Shanxi: the territory of Jizhou in the Yugong.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi lay within the domain of Jizhou as defined in the Yugong.

sentences.zh: 清初沿明制為省，置總督、巡撫。

translations.literal: In the early Qing it was made a province following the Ming system, and a governor-general and a provincial governor were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qing the province was organized along Ming lines, with a governor-general and a provincial governor.

translations.literal: At the end of Shunzhi, the governor-general was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Shunzhi reign the post of governor-general was abolished.

sentences.zh: 康熙四年，並冀南、冀北置雁平道。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kangxi, the Yanping Circuit was established by merging Jizhou South and Jizhou North.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 4 the Yanping circuit was created by combining the former Jizhou South and Jizhou North jurisdictions.

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, the Guihua Sub-prefecture was established.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 the Guihua sub-prefecture was established.

translations.literal: In the second year, eight directly controlled prefectures were added.
translations.idiomatic: The following year eight prefectures were elevated to directly controlled status.

translations.literal: Pingding, Xin, Dai, Bao, Jie, Jiang, Ji, and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Pingding, Xin, Dai, Bao, Jie, Jiang, Ji, and Xi.

translations.literal: In the third year, two prefectures were added.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year two prefectural seats were added.

translations.literal: Ningwu and Shuoping.
translations.idiomatic: Ningwu and Shuoping.

sentences.zh: 六年，升蒲、澤二州並為府，置歸綏道。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the two prefectures Pu and Ze were both promoted to prefectural status, and the Guisui Circuit was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Pu and Ze were both raised to prefectures and the Guisui circuit was created.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四年，增置綏遠廳同知。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qianlong, an associate prefect for the Suiyuan Sub-prefecture was added.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 4 an associate prefect was added at Suiyuan sub-prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，又以歸綏所屬地增置五通判。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, five sub-prefects were further added from territory under Guisui.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year five sub-prefect posts were added from lands under Guisui jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 歸化城、清水河、薩拉齊、和林格爾、托克托城。

translations.literal: Guihua City, Qingshuihe, Salaqi, Horinger, and Tokto City.
translations.idiomatic: Guihua City, Qingshuihe, Salaqi, Horinger, and Tokto City.

sentences.zh: 與歸、綏二廳並屬歸綏道。

translations.literal: Together with the two sub-prefectures Gui and Sui, all were placed under the Guisui Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: These, together with the Gui and Sui sub-prefectures, all came under the Guisui circuit.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，裁歸化城通判。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, the sub-prefect of Guihua City was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year the Guihua City sub-prefect was abolished.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，吉州改屬平陽府，霍州為直隸州。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year, Jizhou was transferred to Pingyang Prefecture, and Huozhou became a directly controlled prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year Jizhou was reassigned to Pingyang prefecture and Huozhou was made a directly controlled prefecture.

sentences.zh: 今領府九，直隸州十，廳十二，州六，縣八十五。

translations.literal: At present it administers nine prefectures, ten directly controlled prefectures, twelve sub-prefectures, six prefectures, and eighty-five counties.
translations.idiomatic: It now comprised nine prefectures, ten directly controlled prefectures, twelve sub-prefectures, six ordinary prefectures, and eighty-five counties.

translations.literal: On the east it bordered Jingxing in Zhili;
translations.idiomatic: To the east it bordered Jingxing in Zhili;

translations.literal: three hundred seventy-five li.
translations.idiomatic: a distance of 375 li.

translations.literal: On the west it bordered Wubu in Shaanxi;
translations.idiomatic: To the west it bordered Wubu in Shaanxi;

translations.literal: five hundred five li.
translations.idiomatic: a distance of 505 li.

translations.literal: On the south it bordered Jiyuan in Henan;
translations.idiomatic: To the south it bordered Jiyuan in Henan;

translations.literal: seven hundred thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: a distance of 730 li.

sentences.zh: 北界內蒙古四子部落草地。

translations.literal: On the north it bordered the pasturelands of the Four Sons tribes in Inner Mongolia.
translations.idiomatic: To the north it bordered the pasturelands of the Four Sons tribes in Inner Mongolia.

translations.literal: one thousand one hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: a distance of 1,100 li.

sentences.zh: 廣八百八十里，袤一千六百二十里。

translations.literal: It was eight hundred eighty li wide and one thousand six hundred twenty li long.
translations.idiomatic: Its breadth was 880 li and its length 1,620 li.

sentences.zh: 北極高三十四度五十七分至四十一度五十分。

translations.literal: North polar altitude ranged from thirty-four degrees fifty-seven minutes to forty-one degrees fifty minutes.
translations.idiomatic: North polar altitude ranged from 34°57′ to 41°50′.

sentences.zh: 京師偏西三度四分至五度四十五分。

translations.literal: West of the capital it ranged from three degrees four minutes to five degrees forty-five minutes.
translations.idiomatic: It lay 3°04′ to 5°45′ west of the capital.

sentences.zh: 東北距京師一千二百里。

translations.literal: Northeast it was one thousand two hundred li from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: From the northeast it was 1,200 li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年，編戶一百九十九萬三十五，口九百二十一萬九千九百八十七。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuantong, registered households numbered one million nine hundred ninety thousand thirty-five, and population nine million two hundred nineteen thousand nine hundred eighty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 3 there were 1,990,035 registered households and a population of 9,219,987.

sentences.zh: 其名山：管涔、太行、王屋、雷首、底柱、析城、恆、霍、句注、五臺。

translations.literal: Its famous mountains: Guanfen, Taihang, Wangwu, Leishou, Dizhu, Xicheng, Heng, Huo, Juzhu, and Wutai.
translations.idiomatic: Notable mountains included Guanfen, Taihang, Wangwu, Leishou, Dizhu, Xicheng, Heng, Huo, Juzhu, and Wutai.

sentences.zh: 其巨川：汾、沁、涑、桑乾、滹沱、清漳、濁漳。

translations.literal: Its great rivers: Fen, Qin, Su, Sanggan, Hutuo, Qingzhang, and Zhuozhang.
translations.idiomatic: Major rivers included the Fen, Qin, Su, Sanggan, Hutuo, Qingzhang, and Zhuozhang.

translations.literal: Railway: Zheng-Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Railway: the Zhengding–Taiyuan line.

sentences.zh: 驛道：西達蒙古、陝西潼關，東北至京師。

translations.literal: Post roads: west reaching Mongolia and Tong Pass in Shaanxi, northeast reaching the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Post roads ran west to Mongolia and Tong Pass in Shaanxi and northeast to the capital.

translations.literal: Telegraph lines reached the capital and Xi'an to the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: Telegraph lines reached the capital and Xi'an to the southwest.

translations.literal: Taiyuan Prefecture: strategic post, populous administration, difficult jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan Prefecture ranked as a strategic post, a populous jurisdiction, and a difficult one to administer.

translations.literal: Subordinate to the Jining Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: It was under the Jining circuit.

sentences.zh: 巡撫，布政、提學、提法司，巡警、勸業道駐。

translations.literal: The provincial governor, the provincial administration, education, and judicial commissioners, and the patrol and industrial promotion circuits were stationed here.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial governor, the commissioners of civil administration, education, and judicial affairs, and the patrol and industrial promotion circuits were all based here.

sentences.zh: 初沿明制，領州五，縣二十。

translations.literal: At first following the Ming system, it administered five prefectures and twenty counties.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, following Ming practice, it governed five prefectures and twenty counties.

sentences.zh: 雍正中，平定、忻、代、保德直隸，割十縣分入之；

translations.literal: During Yongzheng, Pingding, Xin, Dai, and Baode became directly controlled, and ten counties were carved off and assigned to them;
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongzheng, Pingding, Xin, Dai, and Baode were made directly controlled prefectures and ten counties were detached and assigned to them;

translations.literal: soon afterward they were restored to subordination.
translations.idiomatic: but they were soon returned to its jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十八年，省清源入徐溝。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Qianlong, Qingyuan was abolished and merged into Xugou.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 28 Qingyuan was abolished and absorbed into Xugou.

sentences.zh: 距京師千二百里為省治。

translations.literal: One thousand two hundred li from the capital, it served as the provincial seat.
translations.idiomatic: It stood 1,200 li from the capital and served as the provincial capital.

translations.literal: Six hundred li wide and seven hundred li long.
translations.idiomatic: It measured 600 li in breadth and 700 li in length.

sentences.zh: 北極高三十七度五十四分。

translations.literal: North polar altitude thirty-seven degrees fifty-four minutes.
translations.idiomatic: North polar altitude was 37°54′.

sentences.zh: 京師偏西三度五十六分。

translations.literal: Three degrees fifty-six minutes west of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: It lay 3°56′ west of the capital.

translations.literal: It administered one prefecture and ten counties.
translations.idiomatic: It governed one prefecture and ten counties.

translations.literal: Yangqu: strategic post, populous administration, difficult jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Yangqu was classed as strategic, populous, and difficult to govern.

translations.literal: Attached [to the prefectural seat].
translations.idiomatic: Its seat was attached to that of the prefecture.

translations.literal: Northeast: Banquan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast lay Banquan Mountain.

translations.literal: Northwest: Juehan.
translations.idiomatic: To the northwest was Juehan.

translations.literal: North: Lianghong.
translations.idiomatic: To the north was Lianghong.

sentences.zh: 西南：汾水自交城入，逕冽石口，左合埽谷水，折東南，左合洛陰及石橋、真谷水。

translations.literal: Southwest: the Fen River entered from Jiaocheng, passed through Lieshikou, joined on the left with Saogu River, turned southeast, and on the left joined Luoyin and Shiqiao and Zhengu rivers.
translations.idiomatic: To the southwest the Fen entered from Jiaocheng, passed Lieshikou, received Saogu River on the left, turned southeast, and on the left took in the Luoyin, Shiqiao, and Zhengu streams.

sentences.zh: 水經注「逕盂縣、狼孟故城南」者。

translations.literal: This is what the Commentary on the Water Classic describes as "passing Meng County and south of the old city of Langmeng."
translations.idiomatic: This is the stretch the Commentary on the Water Classic describes as passing Meng County and the south of old Langmeng.

sentences.zh: 至城西北，左合石河、南社河，又南入太原。

translations.literal: Reaching the northwest of the city, it joined on the left the Shi and Nanshe rivers, then flowed south into Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the northwest of the city, it received the Shi and Nanshe rivers on the left and continued south into Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 天門關、石嶺關二巡司駐。

translations.literal: Two patrol offices were stationed at Tianmen Pass and Shiling Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Patrol offices were stationed at Tianmen Pass and Shiling Pass.

translations.literal: At Wangfeng Town an associate prefect was stationed.
translations.idiomatic: An associate prefect was posted at Wangfeng Town.

translations.literal: Saoyu Village and Yangxing Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Saoyu Village and Yangxing Stockade.

translations.literal: Chengjing and Lingjing post stations.
translations.idiomatic: The Chengjing and Lingjing courier stations.

translations.literal: Taiyuan: strategic post, populous administration.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan county ranked as strategic and populous.

translations.literal: Forty li southwest of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay forty li southwest of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: Southwest: Jianshan.
translations.idiomatic: To the southwest was Jianshan.

sentences.zh: 西北：蒙山，其南風峪、懸甕，晉水出焉。

translations.literal: Northwest: Meng Mountain; south of it Fengyu and Xuanyu, where the Jin River rises.
translations.idiomatic: To the northwest was Meng Mountain; south of it lay Fengyu and Xuanyu, where the Jin River had its source.

translations.literal: Northeast: Tuoshan.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast was Tuoshan.

sentences.zh: 汾水自陽曲入，左納澗河，逕城東，至南張村與合，又西南入徐溝。

translations.literal: The Fen River entered from Yangqu, received Jian River on the left, passed east of the city, at Nanzhang Village joined with it, then flowed southwest into Xugou.
translations.idiomatic: The Fen entered from Yangqu, took in Jian River on the left, ran east of the city, joined it again at Nanzhang Village, and flowed southwest into Xugou.

sentences.zh: 東：洞渦水自徐溝來，西南流，逕縣南，仍入徐溝界。

translations.literal: East: the Dongwo River came from Xugou, flowed southwest, passed south of the county, and re-entered Xugou territory.
translations.idiomatic: To the east the Dongwo came from Xugou, flowed southwest past the south of the county, and re-entered Xugou.

translations.literal: Yuci: strategic post, populous administration, difficult jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Yuci was classed as strategic, populous, and difficult to govern.

translations.literal: Sixty li southeast of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay sixty li southeast of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: North: Hanshan.
translations.idiomatic: To the north was Hanshan.

translations.literal: Southeast: Lutai.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast was Lutai.

translations.literal: Northeast: Little Wutai.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast was Little Wutai.

sentences.zh: 洞渦水自壽陽入，左納金水河，古塗水，即水經注蒲水，合八賦嶺、鷹山水今所謂大小塗，即水經注蒲谷水注之。

translations.literal: The Dongwo River entered from Shouyang, received on the left the Jinshui River, the ancient Tu River—that is, the Pu River in the Commentary on the Water Classic—which joined the waters of Bafu Ridge and Yingshan, now called the Greater and Lesser Tu, that is, the Pugu River noted in the Commentary on the Water Classic.
translations.idiomatic: The Dongwo entered from Shouyang and on the left took in the Jinshui—the ancient Tu River, identified in the Commentary on the Water Classic as the Pu—which united streams from Bafu Ridge and Yingshan, now known as the Greater and Lesser Tu and corresponding to the Pugu River described in that commentary.

sentences.zh: 右合原過水四派，唐貞觀中，令孫淇引以溉田，逕城南，西南入徐溝。

translations.literal: On the right it joined four branches of the Yuanguo River; in the Zhenguan era of Tang, Magistrate Sun Qi led them to irrigate fields, passed south of the city, and flowed southwest into Xugou.
translations.idiomatic: On the right it received four branches of the Yuanguo; in the Tang Zhenguan reign Magistrate Sun Qi diverted them for irrigation, ran south of the city, and flowed southwest into Xugou.

sentences.zh: 其澗水入蒜谷，又西入太原。

translations.literal: Its stream water entered Suangu Valley, then flowed west into Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Its tributary stream entered Suangu Valley and then flowed west into Taiyuan.

translations.literal: Yuanwo and Shitie, two towns.
translations.idiomatic: The towns of Yuanwo and Shitie.

translations.literal: Mingqian and Wanghu, two post stations.
translations.idiomatic: The Mingqian and Wanghu courier stations.

translations.literal: Taigu: populous administration.
translations.idiomatic: Taigu was classed as populous.

translations.literal: One hundred twenty li southeast of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay 120 li southeast of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: South: Fenghuang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the south was Fenghuang Mountain.

translations.literal: North: Bigu.
translations.idiomatic: To the north was Bigu.

translations.literal: Southeast: Fengchao;
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast were Fengchao;

sentences.zh: 大塔，大塗水出焉，西北流入榆次。

translations.literal: Data; the Greater Tu River rises there and flows northwest into Yuci.
translations.idiomatic: and Data, where the Greater Tu had its source and flowed northwest into Yuci.

sentences.zh: 西：烏馬河自榆社入，右合奄谷水，左咸陽谷水，逕城北入祁。

translations.literal: West: the Wuma River entered from Yushe, joined on the right Yangu River and on the left Xianyang Valley River, passed north of the city, and entered Qi.
translations.idiomatic: To the west the Wuma entered from Yushe, received Yangu River on the right and Xianyang Valley River on the left, passed north of the city, and entered Qi.

sentences.zh: 象谷水即古蔣谷水，入徐溝。

translations.literal: Xianggu River is the ancient Jianggu River; it enters Xugou.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianggu was the ancient Jianggu and flowed into Xugou.

translations.literal: There are Maling Pass and Xinglin Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: It had Maling Pass and Xinglin Stockade.

translations.literal: A registrar was stationed at Fancun Town.
translations.idiomatic: A registrar was posted at Fancun Town.

translations.literal: Qi: strategic post, populous administration.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was classed as strategic and populous.

translations.literal: One hundred forty li southwest of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay 140 li southwest of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: Southeast: Jiefang and Zeshan.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast were Jiefang and Zeshan.

sentences.zh: 侯甲水自武鄉入，逕龍舟峪，為龍舟水。

translations.literal: The Houjia River entered from Wuxiang, passed through Longzhou Valley, and became the Longzhou River.
translations.idiomatic: The Houjia entered from Wuxiang, passed through Longzhou Valley, and was known as the Longzhou River.

sentences.zh: 又盤陀水，西北為昌源渠，逕城北入平遙。

translations.literal: Also the Pantuo River, which to the northwest became the Changyuan Canal, passed north of the city, and entered Pingyao.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the Pantuo, which northwest became the Changyuan Canal, ran north of the city, and entered Pingyao.

sentences.zh: 東北：烏馬河自太谷入，又西入徐溝。

translations.literal: Northeast: the Wuma River entered from Taigu, then flowed west into Xugou.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast the Wuma entered from Taigu and then flowed west into Xugou.

sentences.zh: 子洪、盤陀、團柏、賈令四鎮。

translations.literal: Zihong, Pantuo, Tuanbai, and Jialing, four towns.
translations.idiomatic: The towns of Zihong, Pantuo, Tuanbai, and Jialing.

translations.literal: Anzhai and Pantuo, two post stations.
translations.idiomatic: The Anzhai and Pantuo courier stations.

translations.literal: Xugou: strategic post, populous administration, difficult jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Xugou was classed as strategic, populous, and difficult to govern.

translations.literal: Eighty li south of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay eighty li south of the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十八年省清源為鄉入。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Qianlong, Qingyuan was abolished as a county and entered as a township.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 28 Qingyuan was abolished and absorbed as a township.

translations.literal: The instructor and patrol office were stationed here.
translations.idiomatic: The county instructor and a patrol office were posted here.

translations.literal: West: Huping Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the west was Huping Mountain.

translations.literal: To its north: Baishi and Zhongyin.
translations.idiomatic: To the north lay Baishi and Zhongyin.

sentences.zh: 汾水自太原入，逕孔村至西堡。

translations.literal: The Fen River entered from Taiyuan, passed through Kong Village to Xibao.
translations.idiomatic: The Fen entered from Taiyuan, passed Kong Village, and reached Xibao.

sentences.zh: 東北：洞渦水自榆次入，錯太原，復入縣西，左納烏馬及象河入焉。

translations.literal: Northeast: the Dongwo River entered from Yuci, crossed Taiyuan, re-entered the west of the county, and on the left received the Wuma and Xiang rivers.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast the Dongwo entered from Yuci, crossed Taiyuan, re-entered the western part of the county, and on the left took in the Wuma and Xiang rivers.

translations.literal: Former post-station town.
translations.idiomatic: There was a former post-station town.

translations.literal: Tongge Post Station.
translations.idiomatic: The Tongge courier station.

translations.literal: Jiaocheng: light administration.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaocheng was classed as administratively light.

translations.literal: One hundred twenty li southwest of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay 120 li southwest of the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 交城山，北百二十五里，相近羊腸。

translations.literal: Jiaocheng Mountain, one hundred twenty-five li to the north, lies near Yangchang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaocheng Mountain stood 125 li to the north, near Yangchang.

translations.literal: Northwest: Hutu.
translations.idiomatic: To the northwest was Hutu.

sentences.zh: 汾水自靜樂入，逕火山村，右合孔河，折東入陽曲。

translations.literal: The Fen River entered from Jingle, passed Huoshan Village, joined on the right the Kong River, turned east, and entered Yangqu.
translations.idiomatic: The Fen entered from Jingle, passed Huoshan Village, received the Kong on the right, turned east, and entered Yangqu.

sentences.zh: 西北：孝文山，文水出，會渾谷、西谷，屈東南，左合酸水，為文谷水，入文水界，從之下流，並達之。

translations.idiomatic: To the northwest was Xiaowen Mountain, source of the Wen; it united Hungu and Xigu, bent southeast, took in the Suan on the left to form the Wengu, entered Wenshui, and both streams were reached from its lower course.

translations.literal: Old Jiao Village; a patrol office was stationed there.
translations.idiomatic: At Old Jiao Village a patrol office was posted.

translations.literal: Wenshui: populous administration, difficult jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshui was classed as populous and difficult to govern.

translations.literal: One hundred sixty li southwest of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay 160 li southwest of the prefectural seat.

translations.idiomatic: To the west was Taoshan.

translations.idiomatic: To the northwest was Xionger.

translations.idiomatic: To the southwest was Yinquan.

sentences.zh: 東有汾水，自徐溝入，西南入平遙。

translations.literal: East: the Fen River entered from Xugou and flowed southwest into Pingyao.
translations.idiomatic: To the east the Fen entered from Xugou and flowed southwest into Pingyao.

sentences.zh: 西北：文谷河自交城入，逕文谷口。

translations.literal: Northwest: the Wengu River entered from Jiaocheng and passed Wengukou.
translations.idiomatic: To the northwest the Wengu entered from Jiaocheng and passed Wengukou.

translations.literal: The abandoned canal of Tang Zhacheng was there.
translations.idiomatic: The abandoned canal of Tang Zhacheng lay there.

sentences.zh: 至城北，又東南，左合磁窯河、步渾水，折西南入汾陽。

translations.literal: Reaching north of the city, it turned southeast, joined on the left the Ciyao and Buhun rivers, turned southwest, and entered Fenyang.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the north of the city, it turned southeast, received the Ciyao and Buhun on the left, turned southwest, and entered Fenyang.

translations.literal: There is Xiaoyi Town.
translations.idiomatic: It had Xiaoyi Town.

translations.idiomatic: The present Jiang River rose on the shady slope, flowed east past Shitian Mountain, took in the Gaoli River on the left, then turned northeast, received Shuangze on the right and the Sanjiongshan stream on the left, ran north of the city, and joined the Yi River on the right.

sentences.zh: 雞鳴水乃古諫水，逕余吾故城南、屯留故城北者。

translations.literal: The Jiming River is the ancient Jian River, which passed through south of the old Yuwu city and north of the old Tunliu city.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiming River was the ancient Jian River, which had run south of old Yuwu and north of old Tunliu.

translations.literal: Two garrison towns: Sidi and Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison towns were Sidi and Fengyi.

translations.literal: One post station: Yuwu.
translations.idiomatic: There was one courier station, at Yuwu.

translations.literal: Xiangyuan: strategic post.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyuan was classed as a strategic post.

translations.literal: Ninety li north and slightly west of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay ninety li north and slightly west of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: Southwest: Wucuan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the southwest was Wucuan Mountain.

translations.literal: North: Wuyin and Xiantang.
translations.idiomatic: To the north were Wuyin and Xiantang.

translations.literal: Northwest: Ziyan.
translations.idiomatic: To the northwest was Ziyan.

translations.literal: Southeast: Lutai.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast was Lutai.

sentences.zh: 濁漳水自潞城入，逕其北，左會銅鞮水，又北逕城東。

translations.literal: The Zhang River entered from Lucheng, passed through north of it, left joins the Tongdi River, then north passed through east of the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhang River entered from Lucheng, ran north of the county, took in the Tongdi River on the left, and then flowed north past the east side of the city.

sentences.zh: 東北：涅水自武鄉入，右會臨水，史水自左注之，為合河口，入黎城。

translations.literal: Northeast: the Nie River entered from Wuxiang, right joins the Lin River, the Shi River from the left flows into it, forming Hehekou, and enters Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast the Nie River entered from Wuxiang, joined the Lin River on the right, received the Shi River from the left at Hehekou, and continued into Licheng.

translations.literal: Two garrison towns: Dongzhou and Xialiang.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison towns were Dongzhou and Xialiang.

translations.literal: One post station: Siting.
translations.idiomatic: There was one courier station, at Siting.

translations.literal: Lucheng: light/simple administration.
translations.idiomatic: Lucheng was classed for light, simple administration.

translations.literal: Forty li northeast of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay forty li northeast of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: South: Lushan and Dayu.
translations.idiomatic: To the south were Lushan and Dayu.

translations.literal: Southeast: Funiu and Gejing.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast were Funiu and Gejing.

translations.literal: East: Jinglin.
translations.idiomatic: To the east was Jinglin.

translations.literal: West: Sanchui.
translations.idiomatic: To the west was Sanchui.

translations.literal: Northwest: Huangfu.
translations.idiomatic: To the northwest was Huangfu.

sentences.zh: 西南：濁漳水自屯留入，左合絳水，為交漳，即禹貢降水。

translations.literal: Southwest: the Zhang River entered from Tunliu, left joins the Jiang River, forming Jiaozhang, which is the Jiang River of the Yugong.
translations.idiomatic: To the southwest the Zhang River entered from Tunliu, joined the Jiang River on the left to form Jiaozhang—the Jiang River named in the Yugong.

sentences.zh: 又西北入襄垣，至黎城錯入，逕潞縣故城，是濁漳兼有潞浸之稱。

translations.literal: Then northwest into Xiangyuan; reaching Licheng it enters in crisscross fashion, passed through the old Lucheng county seat—hence the Zhang River also bears the designation of Lu inundation.
translations.idiomatic: It then flowed northwest into Xiangyuan; near Licheng it crossed back and forth, passing the old Lucheng county seat—whence the Zhang River also acquired the name of the Lu inundation.

translations.literal: Then east again crisscrosses Licheng and re-enters the jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: It then turned east, crossed Licheng again, and re-entered the county.

sentences.zh: 東出馬塔口入河南涉縣。

translations.literal: It flows east out through Mata Pass into She County, Henan.
translations.idiomatic: It issued east through Mata Pass into She County in Henan.

translations.literal: Southwest there is Sanchui Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: To the southwest lay Sanchui Ridge.

sentences.zh: 東南有虹梯關，即魯般門，巡司駐。

translations.literal: Southeast there is Hongti Pass, also called Luban Gate, where an inspection office was stationed.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast was Hongti Pass, also known as Luban Gate, where an inspection office was posted.

translations.literal: Three garrison towns: Shentou, Huangnian, and Yangwei.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison towns were Shentou, Huangnian, and Yangwei.

sentences.zh: 東南平順鄉城，鄉學訓導駐焉。

translations.literal: Southeast at Pingshun township seat, where the sub-director of the township school was stationed.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast was the Pingshun township seat, where the sub-director of the township school was posted.

translations.literal: Huguan: light/simple administration.
translations.idiomatic: Huguan was classed for light, simple administration.

translations.literal: Thirty li southeast of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay thirty li southeast of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: Huguan Mountain, six li to the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: Huguan Mountain stood six li to the northwest.

translations.literal: Northeast: Fengxue Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast was Fengxue Mountain.

translations.literal: East: Maju, Maiji, and Angong.
translations.idiomatic: To the east were Maju, Maiji, and Angong.

sentences.zh: 壺水出西北，逕城北為石子河，左合清流河，東南大王、抱犢，又東赤壤。

translations.literal: The Hu River rises in the northwest, passed through north of the city as the Shizi River, left joins the Qingliu River, southeast to Dawang and Baodu, then east to Chirang.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu River rose in the northwest, ran north of the city as the Shizi River, took in the Qingliu River on the left, flowed southeast past Dawang and Baodu, and continued east to Chirang.

sentences.zh: 其陰東井嶺，淘清河出，西北逕黃山，併入長治。

translations.literal: On its shady slope is Dongjing Ridge; the Taoqing River rises there, flows northwest passed through Huangshan, and merges into Changzhi.
translations.idiomatic: On its northern slope lay Dongjing Ridge, where the Taoqing River rose, flowed northwest past Huangshan, and entered Changzhi.

sentences.zh: 嶺東五指河，東南為沾水，逕紫團山入河南林縣。

translations.literal: East of the ridge is the Wuzhi River; southeast it becomes the Zhan River, passed through Zituanshan and enters Lin County, Henan.
translations.idiomatic: East of the ridge was the Wuzhi River, which to the southeast became the Zhan River, passed Zituanshan, and entered Lin County in Henan.

translations.literal: East there is Yuxia Pass.
translations.idiomatic: To the east was Yuxia Pass.

translations.literal: Fengpo Town.
translations.idiomatic: Fengpo Town.

translations.literal: Licheng: light/simple administration.
translations.idiomatic: Licheng was classed for light, simple administration.

translations.literal: One hundred ten li northeast of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay 110 li northeast of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: Southeast: Luci Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast was Luci Mountain.

translations.literal: Northwest: Jibu and Kaiyu.
translations.idiomatic: To the northwest were Jibu and Kaiyu.

sentences.zh: 濁漳水自襄垣入，東南逕聯珠山，錯潞城復入，左合黃須水，東逕赤壁山，仍入之。

translations.literal: The Zhuo Zhang River entered from Xiangyuan, passed southeast through Lianzhu Mountain, crossed Lucheng and re-entered, joined Huangxu River on the left, passed east through Chibi Mountain, and entered again.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuo Zhang entered from Xiangyuan, flowed southeast past Lianzhu Mountain, crossed through Lucheng and back in, received Huangxu River on the left, passed east through Chibi Mountain, and re-entered the county.

sentences.zh: 東北：綉屏，清漳水自遼入，逕吾兒峪，古壺關在焉，入河南涉縣。

translations.literal: Northeast: Xiuping; the Clear Zhang River entered from Liao, passed through Wu'er Valley, where ancient Huguan lay, and entered She County in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast was Xiuping; the Clear Zhang entered from Liao, passed through Wu'er Valley, where ancient Huguan stood, and flowed into She County in Henan.

translations.literal: Yuquan River followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuquan River followed it.

translations.literal: Zezhou Prefecture: strategic post, difficult jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Zezhou Prefecture ranked as a strategic post and a difficult jurisdiction to administer.

translations.literal: Subordinate to the Jining Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: It was under the Jining circuit.

translations.literal: At first following the Ming system, it was a directly controlled prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, following Ming practice, it was organized as a directly controlled prefecture.

translations.literal: It administered four counties.
translations.idiomatic: It governed four counties.

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongzheng it was made a prefecture, and an attached seat county was added.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 6 it was raised to a prefecture and given an attached seat county.

sentences.zh: 西北距省治六百二十里。

translations.literal: Six hundred twenty li northwest from the provincial seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay 620 li northwest of the provincial capital.

translations.literal: One thousand six hundred li to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: It stood 1,600 li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 廣三百四十里，袤二百三十里。

translations.literal: Its breadth was three hundred forty li and its length two hundred thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: It measured 340 li across and 230 li from north to south.

sentences.zh: 北極高三十五度三十一分。

translations.literal: North polar altitude thirty-five degrees thirty-one minutes.
translations.idiomatic: Its north polar altitude was 35°31′.

sentences.zh: 京師偏西三度三十七分。

translations.literal: Three degrees thirty-seven minutes west of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: It lay 3°37′ west of the capital.

translations.literal: It administered five counties.
translations.idiomatic: It governed five counties.

translations.literal: Fengtai: strategic post, populous administration, difficult jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Fengtai was classed as strategic, populous, and difficult to govern.

translations.literal: Attached [to the prefectural seat].
translations.idiomatic: Its seat was attached to that of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 南：太行山，其巔黑石嶺，其北天井關；

translations.literal: South: the Taihang Mountains; their summit was Heishi Ridge, and north of it was Tianjing Pass;
translations.idiomatic: To the south rose the Taihang Mountains; their summit was Heishi Ridge, and to its north stood Tianjing Pass;

sentences.zh: 西南，小口，即太行陘馬牢。

translations.literal: to the southwest, Xiaokou, which is the Taihang Pass Malao.
translations.idiomatic: to the southwest lay Xiaokou, the Taihang Pass known as Malao.

translations.literal: Southeast: Xiashi and Fushan.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast were Xiashi and Fushan.

translations.literal: North: Sima.
translations.idiomatic: To the north was Sima.

sentences.zh: 東北：丹水自高平入，左合蒲水，南逕高都故城東。

translations.literal: Northeast: the Dan River entered from Gaoping, joined Pu River on the left, and flowed south past the east of old Gaodu city.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast the Dan entered from Gaoping, received Pu River on the left, and flowed south past the east side of old Gaodu.

sentences.zh: 其南源澤水，出西北二仙掌，合塔河來會。

translations.literal: Its southern source, the Ze River, issued from northwest Erxianzhang, joined the Ta River, and came to meet it.
translations.idiomatic: Its southern source, the Ze River, rose northwest at Erxianzhang, united with the Ta River, and joined the main stream.

sentences.zh: 又南，左納丈水，逕八盤、壘石、石人山。

translations.literal: Farther south it received Zhang River on the left and passed through Bapan, Leishi, and Shiren mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Farther south it took in Zhang River on the left and passed through Bapan, Leishi, and Shiren mountains.

sentences.zh: 白水合西沙河，逕城南，合轆轤水，天井溪右注之，入河南河內。

translations.literal: Baishui joined the Xisha River, passed south of the city, joined Lulu River, received Tianjing Stream on the right, and entered Henei in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The Baishui united with the Xisha River, ran south of the city, joined the Lulu River, received Tianjing Stream on the right, and flowed into Henei in Henan.

sentences.zh: 西北：吳山，陽阿水出，南逕蟠龍、聖王山，入陽城注沁水。

translations.literal: Northwest: Wushan; Yang'a River issued from it, flowed south past Panlong and Shengwang mountains, entered Yangcheng, and joined the Qin River.
translations.idiomatic: To the northwest was Wushan; the Yang'a rose there, flowed south past Panlong and Shengwang mountains, entered Yangcheng, and joined the Qin River.

translations.literal: The Qin River re-entered and flowed into Wanzi in Jiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin re-entered and flowed into Wanzi in Jiyuan.

translations.literal: Three garrison towns: Hengwang, Lanche, and Zhoucun.
translations.idiomatic: Three garrison towns: Hengwang, Lanche, and Zhoucun.

translations.literal: Two post stations: Taihang and Xingyao.
translations.idiomatic: The Taihang and Xingyao courier stations.

translations.literal: An assistant magistrate and patrol office were stationed at Xingyao.
translations.idiomatic: An assistant magistrate and a patrol office were posted at Xingyao.

translations.literal: Gaoping: strategic post, populous administration.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoping ranked as strategic and populous.

translations.literal: Eighty-five li north-slightly-east of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay eighty-five li north by east of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: North: Hanwang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the north was Hanwang Mountain.

translations.literal: East: Qifo.
translations.idiomatic: To the east was Qifo.

translations.literal: West: Dulu and Haoshan.
translations.idiomatic: To the west were Dulu and Haoshan.

translations.literal: Southwest: Kongcang.
translations.idiomatic: To the southwest was Kongcang.

translations.literal: Northwest: Fajiu; the Zhang River issued from its northern slope.
translations.idiomatic: To the northwest was Fajiu; the Zhang River rose on its northern slope.

sentences.zh: 其巔鳳頭，丹水北源出，左會白水，右絕水，實泫水。

translations.literal: At its summit, Fengtou, the northern source of the Dan River issued, joined Baishui on the left and Jueshui on the right—it was in fact the Xuanshui.
translations.idiomatic: At its summit, Fengtou, the Dan's northern source rose, received Baishui on the left and Jueshui on the right, and was in fact the Xuanshui.

sentences.zh: 東南，右合長平水，逕城北。

translations.literal: Southeastward it joined Changping River on the right and passed north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Flowing southeast, it took in Changping River on the right and passed north of the city.

sentences.zh: 又東南，左合西東長河，至杜村。

translations.literal: Farther southeast it joined Xidong Changhe on the left and reached Ducun.
translations.idiomatic: Farther southeast it received Xidong Changhe on the left and reached Ducun.

sentences.zh: 右合五龍山水，俗亦曰泫水，入鳳臺。

translations.literal: It joined Wulong Mountain River on the right; popularly it was also called the Xuanshui, and it entered Fengtai.
translations.idiomatic: On the right it took in Wulong Mountain River, known locally as the Xuanshui as well, and entered Fengtai.

sentences.zh: 東有蒲水，自陵川入從之。

translations.literal: To the east was Pu River, which entered from Lingchuan and followed it.
translations.idiomatic: To the east the Pu entered from Lingchuan and joined the stream.

translations.literal: To the east was Shibi Pass.
translations.idiomatic: To the east stood Shibi Pass.

translations.literal: To the northwest was Changping Pass.
translations.idiomatic: To the northwest stood Changping Pass.

sentences.zh: 鎮四：米山、丁壁、野川、時庄。

translations.literal: Four garrison towns: Mishan, Dingbi, Yechuan, and Shizhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Four garrison towns: Mishan, Dingbi, Yechuan, and Shizhuang.

translations.literal: The Qiaocun and Changping post stations.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiaocun and Changping courier stations.

translations.literal: Yangcheng: difficult jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Yangcheng was classed as difficult to govern.

translations.literal: Eighty li west of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay eighty li west of the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 西南：王屋，其東析城，有三峰，亦曰底柱，濝水出。

translations.literal: Southwest: Wangwu; east of it was Xicheng, which had three peaks and was also called Dizhu; the Hui River issued there.
translations.idiomatic: To the southwest was Wangwu; east of it stood Xicheng, a three-peaked range also called Dizhu, where the Hui River rose.

sentences.zh: 東南：莽山，溴水出，北源，併入河南濟源。

translations.literal: Southeast: Mangshan; Xiushui issued from it as the northern source and merged into Jiyuan in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast was Mangshan; Xiushui rose there as the northern source and flowed into Jiyuan in Henan.

sentences.zh: 東北：沁水自其縣入，左合史山河，右合陽泉水，東南逕南庄。

translations.literal: Northeast: the Qin River entered from that county, joined Shishan River on the left and Yangquan River on the right, and flowed southeast past Nanzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast the Qin entered from that county, received Shishan River on the left and Yangquan River on the right, and flowed southeast past Nanzhuang.

sentences.zh: 其澗河入為南河，右合濩澤水，逕閻家津，右合桑林水，左納陽阿水，入鳳臺。

translations.literal: Its stream entered as the Nan River, joined Huoze River on the right, passed Yanjiajin, joined Sanglin River on the right, received Yang'a River on the left, and entered Fengtai.
translations.idiomatic: Its stream entered as the Nan River, took in Huoze River on the right, passed Yanjiajin, received Sanglin River on the right and Yang'a River on the left, and entered Fengtai.

sentences.zh: 東南有白雲隘，路通濟源。

translations.literal: To the southeast was Baiyun Pass; the road connected to Jiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast stood Baiyun Pass, on the route to Jiyuan.

translations.literal: Of the seventeen passes in the county, this was the most important.
translations.idiomatic: Among the county's seventeen passes, this was the most critical.

translations.literal: At Dongye Town an associate prefect was stationed.
translations.idiomatic: An associate prefect was posted at Dongye Town.

translations.literal: Lingchuan: light administration.
translations.idiomatic: Lingchuan had light administration.

translations.literal: One hundred twenty li northeast of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay 120 li northeast of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: Southwest: Jiuxian Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the southwest was Jiuxian Mountain.

translations.literal: Northwest: Baoying.
translations.idiomatic: To the northwest was Baoying.

sentences.zh: 聖宮山，蒲水出，屈西，左會龍門山、鳳山水，入高平。

translations.literal: Shenggong Mountain; Pu River issued from it, bent west, joined Longmen Mountain and Fengshan rivers on the left, and entered Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: At Shenggong Mountain the Pu rose, turned west, received Longmen Mountain and Fengshan rivers on the left, and entered Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 東北：堯庄，丈河出，西南逕靈泉、六景、佛兒諸山，入鳳臺。

translations.literal: Northeast: Yaozhuang; Zhang River issued from it, flowed southwest past Lingquan, Liujing, Fo'er, and other mountains, and entered Fengtai.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast at Yaozhuang the Zhang rose, flowed southwest past Lingquan, Liujing, Fo'er, and other mountains, and entered Fengtai.

translations.literal: Southeast: Wangmang Ridge; Yuan River issued from it.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast was Wangmang Ridge, where the Yuan River rose.

sentences.zh: 洪水村，平田水出，併入河南輝縣。

translations.literal: At Hongshui Village Pingtian River issued and merged into Huixian in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: At Hongshui Village the Pingtian rose and flowed into Huixian in Henan.

sentences.zh: 南：雙頭泉，屈南，逕瘦驢嶺入修武。

translations.literal: South: Shuangtou Spring bent south, passed through Shoulü Ridge, and entered Xiuwu.
translations.idiomatic: To the south Shuangtou Spring turned south, passed Shoulü Ridge, and entered Xiuwu.

sentences.zh: 東北：淅山，淇水出，俗淅水，逕熊耳，即沮洳山，入壺關。

translations.literal: Northeast: Xishan; the Qi River issued from it, popularly called Xishui; it passed Xiong'er, which is Juru Mountain, and entered Huguan.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast was Xishan; the Qi rose there, known locally as Xishui; it passed Xiong'er—that is, Juru Mountain—and entered Huguan.

translations.literal: Qinshui: light administration.
translations.idiomatic: Qinshui had light administration.

translations.literal: One hundred seventy li northwest of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay 170 li northwest of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: West: Fushan.
translations.idiomatic: To the west was Fushan.

translations.literal: Southwest: Auxiliary Fushan.
translations.idiomatic: To the southwest was Auxiliary Fushan.

translations.literal: Northeast: Weishan.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast was Weishan.

sentences.zh: 北：大尖，至河頭寨，右合梅河、杏河。

translations.literal: North: Dajian; reaching Hetouzhai, it joined Mei River and Xing River on the right.
translations.idiomatic: To the north was Dajian; at Hetouzhai it received Mei River and Xing River on the right.

sentences.zh: 沁水自岳陽右會東河，即水經黑嶺水。

translations.literal: The Qin River from Yueyang joined Dong River on the right—that is, the Heiling River of the Water Classic.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin from Yueyang received Dong River on the right—the Heiling River of the Water Classic.

sentences.zh: 又東南逕紫金山至端氏故城，左合秦川及熊耳山水，即水經注簳簳水。

translations.literal: Farther southeast it passed Zijin Mountain to old Duanshi city, joined Qinchuan and Xiong'er Mountain rivers on the left—that is, the Jianjian River of the Commentary on the Water Classic.
translations.idiomatic: Farther southeast it passed Zijin Mountain to old Duanshi, took in Qinchuan and Xiong'er Mountain rivers on the left—the Jianjian River of the Commentary on the Water Classic.

sentences.zh: 又東南，左合潘河，入陽城。

translations.literal: Farther southeast it joined Pan River on the left and entered Yangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Farther southeast it received Pan River on the left and entered Yangcheng.

sentences.zh: 西南：鹿臺山，蘆河出，古陽泉水。

translations.literal: Southwest: Lutaishan; Lu River issued from it—the ancient Yangquan River.
translations.idiomatic: To the southwest was Lutaishan; the Lu rose there—the ancient Yangquan River.

translations.literal: Its southern stream also followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Its southern stream joined it as well.

sentences.zh: 鎮四：郭壁、武安、固鎮、端氏。

translations.literal: Four garrison towns: Guobi, Wu'an, Guzhen, and Duanshi.
translations.idiomatic: Four garrison towns: Guobi, Wu'an, Guzhen, and Duanshi.

translations.literal: At Duanshi a patrol office was stationed.
translations.idiomatic: A patrol office was posted at Duanshi.

sentences.zh: 遼州直隸州：繁，隸冀寧道。

translations.literal: Liaozhou Directly Controlled Prefecture: populous administration; subordinate to the Jining Circuit.
